narrative_purpose: Shows why the day measured against the stars (sidereal) is slightly shorter than the day you live by against the sun (synodic): after one full turn relative to the far stars, the whole system has crept along its orbit, so the moon must turn a touch more to bring the sun back overhead.
subject: A gentle two-moment painted scene: the banded gas giant with its small blue-green moon, the whole pair shown at two slightly separated positions along a soft arc around a distant warm sun off toward one edge. In the first position a small surface marking on the moon points straight out at the far stars; in the second, after the system has crept along its arc, that same marking must rotate a little further to point back at the sun.
scene: Deep space from slightly above, a distant warm sun glow toward one edge, faint fixed stars far behind, the planet-moon pair shown at two adjacent positions to imply the small extra turn.
camera: High three-quarters view onto the orbital plane, the two positions side by side so the small extra rotation reads.
light: Warm directional sun glow from one edge; cool indigo space; faint teal on the moon's lit face; the far stars a faint cool dusting.
palette: Void-indigo space, warm sun glow, cream-rust planet bands, teal-cyan moon glow, pale star dusting.
style: Painterly astronomical plate, soft and atmospheric, NOT a hard vector schematic and NOT a render.
detail_level: Moderate: two clear planet-moon positions with a subtly different moon orientation; soft edges; no hard outlines or drawn geometry.
composition: Sun glow toward one edge, the two planet-moon positions along a soft arc across the frame, the moon's surface marking subtly re-aimed between them; generous dark space.
consistency_notes: Same Polyphemus as the cover. The two positions are the same planet-moon pair at two moments, not different objects. The teaching beat is the moon's slightly re-aimed surface marking - keep it subtle and painterly, with no drawn lines or arrows.
negative_prompt: no text, no lettering, no numbers, no labels, no arrows, no drawn orbit lines, no grid, no diagram chrome, no photographic or 3D-render look, no lens flares
